name: Methylphenidate
mechanism: Blocks reuptake of norepinephrine and dopamine and increases their release in the synaptic cleft
dosing: ADHD (children/adolescents): typically 5–20 mg once or twice daily (immediate-release) or 10–60 mg once daily (modified-release) depending on formulation and age; start low and titrate. Narcolepsy: individualized dosing (specialist management). Follow local formularies for age- and weight-specific guidance.
contraindications: Severe hypertension, advanced arteriosclerosis, known structural cardiac abnormalities, hyperthyroidism, glaucoma, current use of MAO inhibitors or within 14 days, known hypersensitivity
interactions: Concurrent sympathomimetics, monoamine oxidase inhibitors (risk of hypertensive crisis), serotonergic drugs (rare serotonin syndrome), antihypertensives may have reduced effect; stimulant effects may be potentiated by other stimulants or anorectics
monitoring: Blood pressure and heart rate before initiation and periodically during treatment; growth (height/weight) in children; psychiatric symptoms (mood, behaviour, psychosis); signs of misuse or diversion
pregnancy: Use only if clearly needed; limited data—discuss risks/benefits with specialist and obstetrics
sideEffects: Insomnia, decreased appetite, weight loss, tachycardia, palpitations, increased blood pressure, anxiety, headache, abdominal pain; rare psychotic symptoms
pharmacokinetics: Well absorbed orally; various formulations (immediate- and modified-release) with differing onset/duration; hepatic metabolism; renal excretion of metabolites
clinicalPearls: Assess cardiac history and perform baseline cardiovascular assessment if risk factors present. Counsel patients about reduced appetite/weight loss in children and timing of doses to reduce insomnia. Monitor for misuse/diversion. Liaise with specialist services for initiation in paediatrics and narcolepsy.
